answer: Give every agent a chip with a silicon fingerprint no two chips share, like a prism splitting light into one pattern only it can make. First, the network sends a random challenge and the chip answers from its microscopic flaws. Second, the chip is re-challenged fresh each epoch, so a copied answer dies on arrival. Third, a second identity from the same chip returns the same fingerprint and collapses into the first. Faking one chip costs $40,000 in lab fabrication, so a thousand fakes cost $40 million, a dune no farm can move grain by grain, while each honest opal keeps its own shine.
